edit: After a refused change, record its terms; the next attempt at that same written change is performed even if it makes some `xrx` asserted.
hypothesis: A refusal record can change later reachability.
falsifier: Every reached result and round agrees with the seventeenth under both answer readings.

edit: A result may be copied as a new alternative, replacing one of its asserted pairs with another pair on the same terms; copying is a change.
hypothesis: Alternatives can inherit with variation.
falsifier: Every copied alternative is already the same result at the same round.

edit: Two alternatives may share a term, and an assertion about a shared term belongs to both alternatives.
hypothesis: Shared terms create effects not seen in disjoint alternatives.
falsifier: The shared-term results factor into separate alternatives at every bounded round.

edit: Each alternative begins with four changes available; each performed change uses one, and no change is performed when none remains. Record how many are left with every result.
hypothesis: A state-carried budget changes reachability beyond the study's round bound.
falsifier: At every recorded budget, the reachable states are the parent's states at the same round.

edit: A reading names at most two terms and records the assertions between them. Two results are the same if every such reading gives the same record.
hypothesis: Sameness by local readings differs from both written equality and FREE rewriting.
falsifier: The bounded partitions agree with one of the parent's two equivalences.

edit: Drop the sentence forbidding `xrx`.
hypothesis: Partial identification and the loop ban ablation fail to commute on reachable loops.
falsifier: The joint closure equals both orders' predicted intersection at equal rounds.
prototype_rejected: The obstruction rule still applies; deletion alone leaves performance of a loop-producing step undecided.

edit: Two results that differ only in how their terms are written are different results.
hypothesis: Written sameness and refusal interact beyond a quotient of the same closure.
falsifier: The written refusal closure is exactly the eighteenth's closure at every round.

edit: An admission that adds an assertion `xrx` is obstructed and refused; record the refusal, which changes nothing.
hypothesis: A feedback record can make the obstruction response change later paths.
falsifier: The admissible record and result counts equal the sixteenth's at each bounded round.
prototype_note: One-term four-round result counts and sets agree with the parent; the refusal removes an edge but its target has a direct-addition path.

edit: Replace the empty beginning with: Given: one change adding a term has been made, and its outcome is the beginning.
hypothesis: A given change shifts reachability and cost without a given assertion.
falsifier: The empty result and one-term result have the ninth's rounds after aligning beginnings.

edit: The two kinds of change are removing a term that names no assertion and removing an assertion. Begin with three terms and one assertion.
hypothesis: Reversing additions gives a terminal partial order with a different obstruction profile.
falsifier: Its bounded result order is the third's reversed order without exceptions.

edit: A leftover is clearable if a sequence of at most two later changes restores the state before it arose; otherwise it is uncleared.
hypothesis: Two-step clearing has outcomes beyond the one-step bare-term criterion.
falsifier: Every two-step clearable leftover was already one-step clearable.

edit: The coarser writing also forgets which term of each assertion was written first.
hypothesis: Forgetting direction adds identifications not generated by relation exchange.
falsifier: Every new coarser class is an old class up to rewriting.

edit: The leftover record is kept with every later result until a later change clears it.
hypothesis: Keeping a record changes result identity and shortest paths.
falsifier: Every tagged result has the parent's cost and unique state tag.

edit: Admitting a result is a change; the empty beginning is admitted, and only an admitted result may undergo another change.
hypothesis: Admission affects future reachability rather than only a tag.
falsifier: The admitted result set and rounds equal the ninth's.

edit: Every recorded change is also a term; an assertion may be written between two recorded changes.
hypothesis: Paths become objects of later assertions.
falsifier: All new assertions can be eliminated without changing any result.

edit: A change between changes is allowed only when every change around their common result is recorded and no such change between them has yet been recorded.
hypothesis: A higher-level boundary condition creates a new obstruction.
falsifier: Every allowed higher change is determined by an ordinary assertion on terms.

edit: Exchanging every `r` assertion with the matching `s` assertion, and conversely, is also a change.
hypothesis: Making the existing involution a step changes shortest paths and sequence counts.
falsifier: All shortest paths and rounds equal the ninth's.

edit: No assertion may have multiplicity greater than two.
hypothesis: A bound on multiplicity makes a fixed-term result set finite and changes frontier completeness.
falsifier: A legal reachable assertion has multiplicity three.

edit: Removing a term that names no assertion is also a change; it deletes that term and nothing asserted.
hypothesis: A bare-term removal destroys the empty state's one-way reachability.
falsifier: No nonempty result reaches the empty beginning within two changes.

edit: Splitting one term into two is also a change; each assertion naming it is copied to both new terms.
hypothesis: A split can reverse an identification without an assertion-by-assertion rebuild.
falsifier: Every split outcome already has a shorter path of the original four kinds.

edit: Adding `xry` is a change only if `xsy` is not asserted, and adding `xsy` only if `xry` is not asserted.
hypothesis: A local cross-relation guard breaks independent addition and may still be bypassed by identification.
falsifier: The guarded and ninth result sets agree in every bounded round.

edit: A change is obstructed whenever its outcome asserts some `xrx`, whether or not that change first made it asserted.
hypothesis: M1 and M2 split on states already asserting a loop.
falsifier: Their attempted-change sets agree on every state with a loop.

edit: Attempt changes that remove fewer assertions before changes that remove more, among changes at the same round.
hypothesis: A third ordering changes the exact frontier under a capped expansion budget.
falsifier: The capped results and frontier match both existing orders.

edit: Only three letters may be used for terms, and adding a term requires an unused letter.
hypothesis: A finite supply yields a genuine last new result rather than a study bound.
falsifier: A result with four terms is reachable.

edit: Record unadmitted leftovers in the order they arose, and admit only the most recent one.
hypothesis: Order-sensitive feedback changes the result quotient and admission paths.
falsifier: All bounded results are classified by the old count alone.

edit: A refused change creates a copy of the same result as a new alternative, with that refusal attached to the copy.
hypothesis: Refusal can vary an alternative without changing its assertions.
falsifier: All copied alternatives are isomorphic under the stated sameness.

edit: Begin with two terms and one `xry` assertion, and nothing written with `s`.
hypothesis: A named nonempty beginning changes which costs survive forgetting names.
falsifier: Every result and cost agrees with the eighth after forgetting names.

edit: For every result, record how many changes were refused on the way to it; two results with different refusal counts are different results.
hypothesis: A refusal trace changes result identity without changing assertions.
falsifier: Every reached state has a unique refusal count at each round.
